title: Audio-Visual Flamingo: Open Audio-Visual Intelligence for Long and Complex Videos
hook: Most audio-visual LLMs only handle short clips. NVIDIA's open AV-Flamingo targets long, real-world video instead — and grounds its reasoning to actual timestamps as it goes.
key_points: Audio-Visual-Skills: ~7M caption and QA training instances from real-world video, built to stress temporal and cross-modal audio-visual reasoning.
Three-stage curriculum trains from short-range perception up to long-horizon, multi-event reasoning.
Temporal Audio-Visual Interleaved Chain-of-Thought grounds each reasoning step to a timestamp in the video, improving alignment and interpretability.
Outperforms similarly-sized open models across 15+ benchmarks and stays competitive with, sometimes beats, much larger open and closed models.
Transfers well to unseen tasks, suggesting the gains generalize rather than being benchmark-specific.
content_html: Audio-visual LLMs have mostly been tuned for short clips. NVIDIA's Audio-Visual Flamingo (AV-Flamingo) instead targets the harder, more realistic case: long, messy real-world videos where understanding what happens depends on tracking sound and image together over time.
extra_html:
Sreyan Ghosh, Wei Ping, and a large NVIDIA-led team build AV-Flamingo around three contributions: Audio-Visual-Skills, a ~7M-instance caption and QA dataset emphasizing temporal, compositional, and cross-modal reasoning; a three-stage curriculum that progresses from short-range perception to long-horizon, multi-event reasoning; and Temporal Audio-Visual Interleaved Chain-of-Thought, which grounds intermediate reasoning steps to timestamps in the video stream rather than reasoning abstractly.

Across more than 15 audio-visual, omni-modal, audio, and vision benchmarks, AV-Flamingo beats similarly-sized open models by clear margins and holds its own against — occasionally surpasses — much larger open-weight and closed models, especially on long, complex real-world video tasks. The authors also report it transfers well to unseen tasks, a sign the gains aren't just benchmark-fitting. Fully open release, described on arXiv, July 2026.

flashcards.prompt: What gap does AV-Flamingo target that prior audio-visual LLMs mostly didn't?
flashcards.back_html: Long and complex real-world videos — prior AV-LLMs mostly handled short clips, while AV-Flamingo is built for long-horizon, multi-event understanding.

flashcards.prompt: What does AV-Flamingo's Temporal Audio-Visual Interleaved Chain-of-Thought do?

choices.text: Grounds intermediate reasoning steps to specific timestamps in the video
Compresses video frames into fewer tokens
Translates audio into text before reasoning begins

flashcards.explanation_html: It's a reasoning framework that explicitly ties each reasoning step to a timestamp in the long audio-visual stream, improving temporal alignment and interpretability.

flashcards.prompt: How does AV-Flamingo's training curriculum progress?
flashcards.back_html: Three stages, moving from short-range perception up to long-horizon, multi-event reasoning, built on ~7M caption/QA instances from real-world video.
